- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 3483-3489
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
  PROBLEM: When the `/contents?ref=${PHASE7_MERGE_BASE_SHA}` request fails due to an API error (not due to the merge-base being unavailable), `phase7_merge_base_blob` defaults to `""` due to `|| echo ""`. The conditional logic `[ "${phase7_base_blob}" != "${phase7_merge_base_blob}" ]` then compares a valid, non-empty `phase7_base_blob` against `""`. This evaluation is true, which triggers an unnecessary call to `_phase7_take_base_version` and an unwanted commit of the base version of a file.
  WHY: An API blip on the merge-base blob request for any file in the PR results in that file being unconditionally overwritten with the base version, creating noisy and spurious commits on the throwaway smoke PR branch, violating the fail-closed requirement for rewrites in this unconflict pass.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 3483-3490 (the `if [ -z "${PHASE7_MERGE_BASE_SHA}" ]` guard added by the last run, in combination with the unchanged `phase7_merge_base_blob=""` initialization at line 3481 and the unchanged `if [ -n "${phase7_base_blob}" ] && [ "${phase7_base_blob}" != "${phase7_merge_base_blob}" ]` rewrite condition)
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
  PROBLEM: The fail-closed guard added by the last run only handles one of the two ways the merge-base information can be unknown. When `/compare` succeeds and returns a non-empty `PHASE7_MERGE_BASE_SHA`, but the subsequent `gh api "repos/${TEST_REPO}/contents/${phase7_path}?ref=${PHASE7_MERGE_BASE_SHA}"` call fails for one path inside the loop, `phase7_merge_base_blob` retains its initialised `""` (the call is wrapped in `--jq '.sha // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo ""`). The rewrite condition then evaluates `[ -n "${phase7_base_blob}" ]` true and `[ "${phase7_base_blob}" != "${phase7_merge_base_blob}" ]` true (any non-empty blob differs from `""`), so `_phase7_take_base_version` rewrites that file with the base version and pushes a `[E2E Smoke Test] take <base> version of <path>` commit — even though we cannot confirm the base actually changed that path since the merge base.
  WHY: The per-file merge-base blob API call can fail independently of the `/compare` call (transient network error, per-call rate limiting, GitHub-side error). In a smoke PR whose file list overlaps with the base on more than a handful of paths, the loop can easily hit one failed blob fetch on a non-conflict-relevant file. That file will then receive a noisy `[E2E Smoke Test] take <base> version of <path>` commit, violating the changelog's "overlap-only rewrite rule" and the PR description's "on a conflict it overwrites each PR file the base also changed with the base's version" contract. The fail-closed invariant the last autofix was supposed to enforce still has a hole.
- tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_phase7_unconflict.py

  SEVERITY: NIT

  PROBLEM: The contract test asserts the `merge_base_unavailable` branch but does not pin a parallel branch for the per-file `phase7_merge_base_blob` fetch-failed case.
  WHY: Without that guard in the workflow, the only way to verify a future autofix retains the fail-closed invariant for both ways the merge base can be unknown is by re-reading the implementation, which is the regression the last autofix demonstrated.

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 3481-3488 (the per-file merge-base blob fetch and the subsequent guard)
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
  PROBLEM: The fail-closed guard the last run added (`if [ -z "${PHASE7_MERGE_BASE_SHA}" ]`) only covers the case where `/compare` yields no merge-base SHA. When `/compare` succeeds (SHA is set) but the per-file `gh api "repos/${TEST_REPO}/contents/${phase7_path}?ref=${PHASE7_MERGE_BASE_SHA}"` call at line 3483 fails — an API blip, transient 5xx, or a 404 for a path absent at the merge base — `phase7_merge_base_blob` stays at its initialised `""` (the call is wrapped in `--jq '.sha // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo ""`). The next check then runs: `if [ -z "${PHASE7_MERGE_BASE_SHA}" ]` is FALSE (the SHA is set), so control falls to `elif [ -n "${phase7_base_blob}" ] && [ "${phase7_base_blob}" != "${phase7_merge_base_blob}" ]`. Any non-empty base blob differs from `""`, so the comparison succeeds and `_phase7_take_base_version` rewrites the file with the base's version even though the code could not confirm the base actually changed the file since the merge base. This is the same fail-open spurious-rewrite class the prior reviewer finding called out; the last run moved the trigger from "compare failed" to "merge-base blob fetch failed" without closing it.
  WHY: A transient GitHub API failure on the merge-base blob request in any per-file loop iteration pushes a `[E2E Smoke Test] take <base> version of <path>` commit to the throwaway smoke branch for a file that may not have been conflict-relevant, violating the "only rewrites files the base changed since merge base" invariant the contract test `test_unconflict_only_rewrites_files_the_base_changed_since_merge_base` asserts. The fix is a one-line extension of the existing guard: `if [ -z "${PHASE7_MERGE_BASE_SHA}" ] || [ -z "${phase7_merge_base_blob}" ]; then` — treat a failed merge-base blob fetch the same as an unavailable merge base.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
